title: Distributed Training
description: Distributed training: Birden fazla GPU/node ile paralel training. Data parallelism (batch split), model parallelism (model split), pipeline parallelism. Multi-GPU, multi-node. Large models (GPT, LLaMA), faster training.

content.level0_basic: Distributed Training, birden fazla GPU/node kullanarak model training'i hızlandırır. Single GPU problem: Large models (GPT-3: 175B params, 700GB memory) GPU memory'ye sığmaz. Training slow (days-weeks). Çözüm: (1) **Data Parallelism**: Batch'i split et (her GPU aynı model, farklı data). Gradients sync (AllReduce). Linear speedup (ideal: 8 GPU → 8x faster). (2) **Model Parallelism**: Model'i split et (her GPU model'in parçası). Large models GPU'ya sığar. (3) **Pipeline Parallelism**: Layers'ı stages'e böl (pipeline), micro-batches. Bubble minimize. Communication: Collective ops (AllReduce, AllGather, Broadcast). Bandwidth critical (NVLink, InfiniBand).
content.level1_beginner: Parallelism türleri: (1) **Data Parallelism (DP)**: Her GPU full model replica (sync weights). Batch split (örn: batch=256, 8 GPU → 32/GPU). Forward/backward local, gradients AllReduce (average), optimizer step. Sync: Synchronous (wait all GPUs), Asynchronous (no wait, stale gradients). PyTorch DistributedDataParallel (DDP). (2) **Model Parallelism (MP)**: Model split across GPUs (layers veya tensor). Tensor parallelism (matrix multiply split), pipeline parallelism (layers to stages). Memory ↓, communication ↑. (3) **Pipeline Parallelism**: Layers → stages (GPU1: L1-L5, GPU2: L6-L10). Micro-batches (pipeline fill), F-then-B schedule (forward all, then backward). Bubble time (idle). (4) **Hybrid**: DP + MP + Pipeline. GPT-3 (DP=64, MP=8, Pipeline=4). (5) **Gradient Accumulation**: Simulate large batch (small batches accumulate, single optimizer step). Memory efficient. Frameworks: PyTorch DDP, DeepSpeed, Megatron-LM, Horovod, JAX pmap.
content.level2_application: Pratik uygulamalar: (1) **Large Language Models**: GPT-3 (175B), LLaMA (70B), BLOOM (176B). 3D parallelism (DP×MP×Pipeline). DeepSpeed ZeRO (optimizer state split). Training: Weeks (thousands of GPUs). (2) **Computer Vision**: ResNet, ViT training (ImageNet). Data parallelism (8-64 GPUs). Batch size scaling (linear scaling rule: LR ∝ batch size). (3) **Recommendation Systems**: Large embedding tables (billions of params). Model parallelism (embedding split). Meta, Google ads. (4) **Research**: Multi-GPU workstations (4-8 GPUs, NVLink). Academic labs. PyTorch DDP (simple setup). (5) **Cloud Training**: AWS (p4d.24xlarge: 8×A100), GCP (a2-megagpu-16g), Azure (ND96asr_v4). Auto-scaling, spot instances. (6) **Fine-tuning**: Pre-trained models (BERT, GPT) → fine-tune (smaller data, fewer GPUs). LoRA (parameter-efficient). Tools: PyTorch Lightning (DDP abstraction), Accelerate (Hugging Face), Ray Train, TensorFlow MultiWorkerMirroredStrategy.
content.level3_advanced: İleri seviye: (1) **ZeRO (Zero Redundancy Optimizer)**: DeepSpeed. ZeRO-1 (optimizer states split), ZeRO-2 (+ gradients split), ZeRO-3 (+ parameters split). Memory: O(Ψ/N) (N=GPUs). Trillion-param models. (2) **Tensor Parallelism**: Matrix multiply split (Megatron-LM). A·B = [A1, A2]·[B1; B2]. AllReduce after. Column/row parallel. Intra-layer. (3) **Pipeline Schedules**: GPipe (synchronous, bubble ~50%), PipeDream (asynchronous, stale weights), 1F1B (one-forward-one-backward, bubble ~10%). Micro-batch size tuning. (4) **Mixed Precision**: FP16/BF16 (training), FP32 (master weights). Memory ↓ (2x), speed ↑ (2-3x, Tensor Cores). Loss scaling (prevent underflow). (5) **Gradient Compression**: Top-k sparsification, quantization (1-bit). Communication ↓, accuracy trade-off. Error feedback (compensate compression error). (6) **Asynchronous SGD**: No sync wait, stale gradients. Faster (no blocking), convergence slower. Hogwild!, Downpour SGD. (7) **Elastic Training**: Dynamic GPUs (add/remove). Fault tolerance (GPU failure). PyTorch Elastic, Horovod Elastic.
content.level4_expert: Expert seviyede, system optimization, large-scale clusters ve research frontiers önemlidir. (1) **Communication Optimization**: (a) Overlapping (computation + communication). (b) Gradient bucketing (reduce small AllReduce calls). (c) Hierarchical AllReduce (NVLink intra-node, InfiniBand inter-node). (d) Ring AllReduce vs Tree AllReduce. (2) **Large-Scale Clusters**: 1000+ GPUs. Network topology (leaf-spine, fat-tree). Bandwidth (100-400 Gbps InfiniBand). Collective tuning (NCCL parameters). Job scheduling (SLURM, Kubernetes). (3) **Checkpointing**: Activation checkpointing (recompute forward, save memory). Gradient checkpointing (selective). Distributed checkpointing (parallel save/load). (4) **Profiling**: PyTorch Profiler, NVIDIA Nsight. Communication bottlenecks, GPU utilization, memory usage. Optimization: Batch size, micro-batch, gradient accumulation. (5) **Heterogeneous Training**: CPU + GPU + TPU. Different hardware (A100 + V100). Load balancing. (6) **Federated Learning**: Distributed data (privacy). Aggregation (FedAvg). Communication-efficient (compression, local steps). (7) **MoE (Mixture of Experts)**: Conditional computation. Expert parallelism (experts to GPUs). Routing (top-k experts). GShard, Switch Transformer. Research: **FlashAttention distributed**, **Automatic parallelization** (Alpa, GSPMD), **Communication-avoiding algorithms**, **Disaggregated training** (compute + memory separation), **Carbon-aware training** (schedule for low-carbon periods).

whatIsIt: Distributed Training: Multiple GPUs/nodes paralel training. Data parallelism: Replica models, split batch, sync gradients (AllReduce). Model parallelism: Split model (tensor/pipeline). Matematiksel: Speedup = T_single / T_distributed (ideal: linear, N GPUs → N× speedup). Communication: AllReduce O(N·M) (N=GPUs, M=model size), Ring AllReduce O(M). Efficiency = (T_compute / (T_compute + T_communicate)). Scalability: Strong scaling (fixed problem, more GPUs → faster), weak scaling (problem size ∝ GPUs).
whyNeeded: Distributed training kritik çünkü: (1) **Large Models**: GPT-3 (175B, 700GB), LLaMA (70B, 280GB). Single GPU (A100: 80GB) sığmaz. Model parallelism gerekli. (2) **Training Speed**: Single GPU: ImageNet (ResNet-50) ~7 days. 8 GPU: ~1 day (7x speedup). 64 GPU: ~3 hours. Time-to-market critical. (3) **Cost**: Cloud GPU expensive ($2-10/hour). Faster training → cheaper (7 days → 1 day = 7x cost ↓). Spot instances (3-10x cheaper). (4) **Experimentation**: Hyperparameter search, architecture search. Multiple runs parallel (10 configs × 8 GPUs = 80 GPUs, finish in hours). (5) **Scale Laws**: Larger models → better performance (GPT-3 > GPT-2). Scaling requires distributed (impossible otherwise). (6) **Research Competition**: SOTA models require thousands of GPUs (Meta LLaMA: 2048 A100, 21 days). Academic/industry gap. (7) **Batch Size**: Large batch (better GPU utilization, Tensor Cores). Single GPU limited (memory). Distributed: scale batch (linear scaling rule).
realWorldAnalogy: Distributed training'i fabrika üretimine benzetebiliriz. **Single GPU (tek işçi)**: Araba üret (start-to-finish, 1 araba/gün). Slow, limited capacity. **Data Parallelism (çok işçi, aynı task)**: 8 işçi, her biri ayrı araba üret (aynı blueprint). 8x faster (8 araba/gün). Communication: Günlük meeting (blueprint update sync). Sync: Herkes finish etmeli → next day (synchronous). Async: Herkes kendi hızında, blueprint sometimes outdated (asynchronous, stale). **Model Parallelism (assembly line)**: Araba'yı parçalara böl (GPU1: motor, GPU2: gövde, GPU3: tekerlekler). Her işçi specialized. Memory: Büyük araba → single işçi handle edemez, split gerekir. Communication: Parts transfer (inter-GPU). **Pipeline Parallelism (conveyor belt)**: 3 stage (motor → gövde → tekerlekler). Micro-batches (3 araba aynı anda, farklı stages). Stage 1 finish motor → Stage 2 başlar gövde (parallel work). Bubble: Stage 3 bekler (initial fill time). **Hybrid (factory optimize)**: 24 işçi = 3 assembly lines (pipeline) × 8 işçiler/line (data parallel). Optimize throughput. **Communication**: Blueprint sync (gradients AllReduce), parts transfer (activations). Bandwidth: Highway (NVLink: fast, InfiniBand: inter-factory). Bottleneck: Slow highway → idle time.

formulas: \text{Speedup}: \quad S = \frac{T_{\text{single}}}{T_{\text{distributed}}} \quad \text{(ideal: S = N for N GPUs)}
\text{AllReduce Time}: \quad T_{\text{AllReduce}} = 2 \cdot (N-1) \cdot \frac{M}{B} \quad \text{(naive, N=GPUs, M=model size, B=bandwidth)}
\text{ZeRO Memory}: \quad \text{Memory}_{\text{ZeRO-3}} = \frac{\Psi + K \cdot \Psi}{N} \quad \text{(Ψ=params, K=optimizer states factor, N=GPUs)}

stepByStep: 1. **Problem Assessment**: Model size (params, memory), dataset size (samples), GPU resources (count, memory, interconnect). Single GPU feasible? (model+batch fit in 80GB A100?). If no → model parallelism. If slow → data parallelism.

2. **Parallelism Strategy Selection**: (a) Model fits single GPU, want faster: Data parallelism (DDP). (b) Model too large (>80GB): Model parallelism (tensor, pipeline) or ZeRO-3. (c) Very large (GPT-3): 3D parallelism (DP × MP × Pipeline). (d) Limited bandwidth: Gradient compression, mixed precision.

3. **Data Parallelism Setup (PyTorch DDP)**: (a) Init process group (torch.distributed.init_process_group, backend='nccl' for GPU). (b) Wrap model (DDP(model, device_ids=[local_rank])). (c) Split dataset (DistributedSampler, each GPU different subset). (d) Training loop: Forward/backward local, gradients auto-sync (AllReduce), optimizer step. (e) Batch size: Global batch = per_GPU_batch × N_GPUs.

4. **Model Parallelism Setup**: (a) Tensor parallelism: Split layers (linear: weight columns, Megatron-LM). AllReduce after. (b) Pipeline parallelism: Split model to stages (layers → GPUs). Micro-batches (batch split). Forward stage-by-stage, backward reverse. Schedule: GPipe (sync), 1F1B (overlap). (c) Activation checkpointing (memory save).
5. **Mixed Precision**: torch.cuda.amp (Automatic Mixed Precision). FP16 forward/backward (Tensor Cores), FP32 master weights. GradScaler (loss scaling, prevent underflow). 2x memory ↓, 2-3x speed ↑.

6. **Communication Optimization**: (a) Gradient bucketing (DDP default, 25MB buckets). (b) Overlapping: Backward compute + AllReduce (async). (c) find_unused_parameters=False (DDP, faster if no unused). (d) NCCL tuning (environment variables, NCCL_DEBUG=INFO for profiling).

7. **Hyperparameter Scaling**: (a) Batch size: Linear scaling rule (LR ∝ batch). Warmup (gradual LR increase, first few epochs). (b) Gradient accumulation: Effective batch = micro_batch × accumulation_steps × N_GPUs. Simulate large batch (memory efficient). (c) Validation: Same global batch (reproducibility).

8. **Monitoring**: (a) GPU utilization (nvidia-smi, 80-95% target). (b) Communication time (PyTorch Profiler, <20% total time ideal). (c) Memory usage (per GPU). (d) Throughput (samples/sec, images/sec). (e) Loss convergence (same as single GPU?).

9. **Checkpointing**: (a) Distributed: Only rank 0 save (full model). Or: Each rank save shard (model parallelism). (b) Frequency: Every N steps, on_eval. (c) Resume: Load checkpoint, restore optimizer state, LR scheduler. Fault tolerance.

10. **Scaling Testing**: (a) Strong scaling: Fixed problem (dataset), increase GPUs (2, 4, 8, 16). Measure speedup (ideal: linear). (b) Weak scaling: Problem size ∝ GPUs (batch size ×2). Time constant (ideal). (c) Bottleneck: Communication? (bandwidth upgrade, gradient compression). Computation? (GPU upgrade, mixed precision).
algorithm.complexity: **Zaman Karmaşıklığı**: Single GPU: O(B·F + B·B_backward) per step (B=batch, F=forward, B_backward=backward). Data parallelism: O(B/N·F + B/N·B_backward + AllReduce) (N=GPUs). AllReduce: Ring O(M/B_bandwidth) (M=model size). Ideal speedup: N× (communication << computation). **Communication**: AllReduce dominant (O(model size)). Bandwidth: NVLink (300-600 GB/s intra-node), InfiniBand (100-400 Gbps inter-node). Model parallelism: Activation transfer O(batch·hidden_dim). **Uzay**: Data parallelism: O(model + optimizer) per GPU (replica). Model parallelism: O(model/N + activations). ZeRO-3: O(model/N + optimizer/N). **Scalability**: Near-linear (2-16 GPUs, good interconnect). Sub-linear (>64 GPUs, communication overhead ↑). Weak scaling better (batch size ↑).

codeExamples.title: PyTorch DistributedDataParallel (DDP)
codeExamples.code:
import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.distributed as dist
from torch.nn.parallel import DistributedDataParallel as DDP
from torch.utils.data import DataLoader, DistributedSampler
import os

def setup(rank, world_size):
    """Initialize process group"""
    os.environ['MASTER_ADDR'] = 'localhost'
    os.environ['MASTER_PORT'] = '12355'
    dist.init_process_group('nccl', rank=rank, world_size=world_size)

def cleanup():
    dist.destroy_process_group()

def train(rank, world_size):
    print(f'Running DDP on rank {rank} (world_size={world_size})')
    setup(rank, world_size)
    
    # Model
    model = nn.Linear(100, 10).to(rank)
    ddp_model = DDP(model, device_ids=[rank])
    
    # Dummy data
    dataset = torch.randn(1000, 100)
    labels = torch.randint(0, 10, (1000,))
    
    # DistributedSampler (each GPU gets different subset)
    sampler = DistributedSampler(dataset, num_replicas=world_size, rank=rank)
    dataloader = DataLoader(dataset, batch_size=32, sampler=sampler)
    
    # Training
    optimizer = torch.optim.SGD(ddp_model.parameters(), lr=0.01)
    criterion = nn.CrossEntropyLoss()
    
    ddp_model.train()
    for epoch in range(3):
        sampler.set_epoch(epoch)  # Shuffle differently each epoch
        for batch_idx, data in enumerate(dataloader):
            data = data.to(rank)
            # Note: labels would come from dataloader in real scenario
            
            optimizer.zero_grad()
            outputs = ddp_model(data)
            loss = criterion(outputs, torch.randint(0, 10, (len(data),)).to(rank))
            loss.backward()  # Gradients auto-sync via AllReduce
            optimizer.step()
            
            if rank == 0 and batch_idx % 10 == 0:
                print(f'Epoch {epoch}, Batch {batch_idx}, Loss: {loss.item():.4f}')
    
    cleanup()

# Run (normally via torch.multiprocessing.spawn or torchrun)
if __name__ == '__main__':
    world_size = 2  # 2 GPUs
    # torch.multiprocessing.spawn(train, args=(world_size,), nprocs=world_size)
    print('Example: torchrun --nproc_per_node=2 script.py')
    print('DDP: Data parallelism, gradients auto-sync (AllReduce)')
codeExamples.explanation: PyTorch DDP: Data parallelism. DistributedSampler (each GPU different data). Gradients auto-sync (AllReduce). Launch: torchrun or mp.spawn.

codeExamples.title: Gradient Accumulation (Simulate Large Batch)
codeExamples.code:
import torch
import torch.nn as nn

# Model
model = nn.Linear(100, 10).cuda()
optimizer = torch.optim.SGD(model.parameters(), lr=0.01)
criterion = nn.CrossEntropyLoss()

# Params
micro_batch_size = 32
accumulation_steps = 4
effective_batch_size = micro_batch_size * accumulation_steps

print(f'Micro-batch: {micro_batch_size}')
print(f'Accumulation steps: {accumulation_steps}')
print(f'Effective batch size: {effective_batch_size}')

# Dummy data
data = torch.randn(effective_batch_size, 100).cuda()
labels = torch.randint(0, 10, (effective_batch_size,)).cuda()

# Training with gradient accumulation
model.train()
optimizer.zero_grad()

for i in range(accumulation_steps):
    # Micro-batch
    start = i * micro_batch_size
    end = start + micro_batch_size
    micro_data = data[start:end]
    micro_labels = labels[start:end]
    
    # Forward
    outputs = model(micro_data)
    loss = criterion(outputs, micro_labels)
    
    # Backward (accumulate gradients)
    loss = loss / accumulation_steps  # Average loss
    loss.backward()
    
    print(f'Step {i+1}/{accumulation_steps}, Loss: {loss.item()*accumulation_steps:.4f}')

# Optimizer step (single update after accumulation)
optimizer.step()
optimizer.zero_grad()

print('\nGradient accumulation: Simulate large batch, memory efficient')
print('Effective batch = micro_batch × accumulation_steps')
print('Use case: Large batch on limited memory GPU')
codeExamples.explanation: Gradient Accumulation: Simulate large batch (memory efficient). Multiple micro-batches, accumulate gradients, single optimizer step. Effective batch size ↑.

codeExamples.title: Mixed Precision Training (AMP)
codeExamples.code:
import torch
import torch.nn as nn
from torch.cuda.amp import autocast, GradScaler
import time

# Model
model = nn.Sequential(
    nn.Linear(1024, 2048),
    nn.ReLU(),
    nn.Linear(2048, 512),
    nn.ReLU(),
    nn.Linear(512, 10)
).cuda()

optimizer = torch.optim.Adam(model.parameters(), lr=0.001)
criterion = nn.CrossEntropyLoss()
scaler = GradScaler()  # For loss scaling

# Dummy data
data = torch.randn(256, 1024).cuda()
labels = torch.randint(0, 10, (256,)).cuda()

print('=== Mixed Precision Training ===')

# FP32 training
model.train()
start = time.time()
for step in range(100):
    optimizer.zero_grad()
    outputs = model(data)
    loss = criterion(outputs, labels)
    loss.backward()
    optimizer.step()
fp32_time = time.time() - start

print(f'FP32 training (100 steps): {fp32_time:.2f}s')

# FP16 training (AMP)
start = time.time()
for step in range(100):
    optimizer.zero_grad()
    
    # Forward in FP16
    with autocast():
        outputs = model(data)
        loss = criterion(outputs, labels)
    
    # Backward with scaled loss
    scaler.scale(loss).backward()
    scaler.step(optimizer)
    scaler.update()

fp16_time = time.time() - start

print(f'FP16 training (AMP, 100 steps): {fp16_time:.2f}s')
print(f'Speedup: {fp32_time/fp16_time:.2f}x')
print('\nAMP: FP16 forward/backward (Tensor Cores), FP32 master weights')
print('Loss scaling: Prevent underflow. 2-3x faster, 2x memory saving')
codeExamples.explanation: Mixed Precision (AMP): FP16 compute (Tensor Cores), FP32 master weights. GradScaler (loss scaling). 2-3x speedup, 2x memory ↓. torch.cuda.amp.

codeExamples.title: Model Parallelism (Simple Pipeline)
codeExamples.code:
import torch
import torch.nn as nn

# Model split across 2 GPUs (pipeline)
class PipelineModel(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__()
        # Stage 1: GPU 0
        self.stage1 = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(1024, 2048),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Linear(2048, 1024)
        ).to('cuda:0')
        
        # Stage 2: GPU 1
        self.stage2 = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(1024, 512),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Linear(512, 10)
        ).to('cuda:1')
    
    def forward(self, x):
        # Stage 1 on GPU 0
        x = x.to('cuda:0')
        x = self.stage1(x)
        
        # Transfer to GPU 1
        x = x.to('cuda:1')
        x = self.stage2(x)
        
        return x

# Check GPUs
if torch.cuda.device_count() < 2:
    print('Need 2 GPUs for this example (simulating with 1)')
    # Fallback: Use same GPU
    model = nn.Sequential(
        nn.Linear(1024, 2048),
        nn.ReLU(),
        nn.Linear(2048, 1024),
        nn.Linear(1024, 512),
        nn.ReLU(),
        nn.Linear(512, 10)
    ).cuda()
else:
    model = PipelineModel()
    print('Pipeline model: Stage 1 (GPU 0), Stage 2 (GPU 1)')

# Dummy data
data = torch.randn(32, 1024)
labels = torch.randint(0, 10, (32,))

if torch.cuda.device_count() >= 2:
    labels = labels.to('cuda:1')  # Final GPU
else:
    labels = labels.cuda()

optimizer = torch.optim.Adam(model.parameters(), lr=0.001)
criterion = nn.CrossEntropyLoss()

# Training
model.train()
for epoch in range(3):
    optimizer.zero_grad()
    outputs = model(data)
    loss = criterion(outputs, labels)
    loss.backward()
    optimizer.step()
    
    print(f'Epoch {epoch+1}, Loss: {loss.item():.4f}')

print('\nModel Parallelism: Model split across GPUs')
print('Use case: Large model (doesn\'t fit single GPU)')
print('Communication: Activations transfer between stages')
codeExamples.explanation: Model Parallelism: Model split across GPUs (pipeline stages). Stage 1 (GPU 0), Stage 2 (GPU 1). Activation transfer. Large models fit.

codeExamples.title: Communication Profiling
codeExamples.code:
import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.distributed as dist
from torch.profiler import profile, ProfilerActivity
import time

# Simulate AllReduce (collective communication)
def benchmark_allreduce(size_mb, world_size=4):
    """
    Benchmark AllReduce communication
    size_mb: Tensor size in MB
    """
    # Tensor
    tensor_size = int(size_mb * 1024 * 1024 / 4)  # 4 bytes per float32
    tensor = torch.randn(tensor_size).cuda()
    
    # Warmup
    for _ in range(10):
        # Simulate AllReduce (in real: dist.all_reduce(tensor))
        _ = tensor.mean()
    
    torch.cuda.synchronize()
    
    # Benchmark
    start = time.time()
    for _ in range(100):
        # Simulate: In DDP, this is automatic gradient sync
        _ = tensor.mean()  # Placeholder for AllReduce
    
    torch.cuda.synchronize()
    elapsed = time.time() - start
    
    return elapsed / 100

print('=== Communication Profiling ===')
print('(Simulated AllReduce timing)\n')

sizes_mb = [1, 10, 100, 500]  # Model sizes
for size in sizes_mb:
    time_ms = benchmark_allreduce(size) * 1000
    bandwidth = size / (time_ms / 1000)  # MB/s
    print(f'Model size: {size} MB')
    print(f'  AllReduce time: {time_ms:.2f} ms')
    print(f'  Effective bandwidth: {bandwidth:.1f} MB/s')
    print()

print('Real DDP: Use PyTorch Profiler')
print('Example:')
print('with profile(activities=[ProfilerActivity.CPU, ProfilerActivity.CUDA]) as prof:')
print('    # Training loop')
print('print(prof.key_averages().table())')
print('\nCheck: NCCL communication time vs compute time (<20% ideal)')
codeExamples.explanation: Communication Profiling: Benchmark AllReduce (gradient sync). Measure time, bandwidth. PyTorch Profiler: CPU/CUDA activity. Optimize: <20% communication.

codeExamples.title: Scaling Efficiency Analysis
codeExamples.code:
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np

# Simulate scaling experiment
num_gpus = [1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32]

# Ideal: Linear speedup
ideal_speedup = num_gpus

# Real: Sub-linear (communication overhead)
real_speedup = [1, 1.9, 3.7, 7.2, 13.5, 24.0]

# Efficiency
efficiency = [r / n for r, n in zip(real_speedup, num_gpus)]

# Plot
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(14, 5))

# Speedup
ax = axes[0]
ax.plot(num_gpus, ideal_speedup, 'k--', label='Ideal (Linear)', linewidth=2)
ax.plot(num_gpus, real_speedup, 'ro-', label='Real', linewidth=2, markersize=8)
ax.set_xlabel('Number of GPUs')
ax.set_ylabel('Speedup')
ax.set_title('Strong Scaling: Speedup vs GPUs')
ax.legend()
ax.grid(alpha=0.3)
ax.set_xscale('log', base=2)
ax.set_yscale('log', base=2)

# Efficiency
ax = axes[1]
ax.plot(num_gpus, efficiency, 'bs-', linewidth=2, markersize=8)
ax.axhline(1.0, color='k', linestyle='--', label='100% Efficient')
ax.set_xlabel('Number of GPUs')
ax.set_ylabel('Efficiency (Speedup / N)')
ax.set_title('Scaling Efficiency')
ax.legend()
ax.grid(alpha=0.3)
ax.set_xscale('log', base=2)

plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

print('=== Scaling Analysis ===')
for i, n in enumerate(num_gpus):
    print(f'{n} GPUs: Speedup={real_speedup[i]:.1f}x (ideal={ideal_speedup[i]}x), Efficiency={efficiency[i]*100:.1f}%')

print('\nInsights:')
print('1. Near-linear scaling (2-8 GPUs): Good interconnect (NVLink)')
print('2. Sub-linear (16+ GPUs): Communication overhead ↑')
print('3. Efficiency drop: 95% (8 GPUs) → 75% (32 GPUs)')
print('4. Bottleneck: Inter-node bandwidth (InfiniBand), AllReduce cost')
print('\nOptimization: Gradient compression, pipeline parallelism, mixed precision')
codeExamples.explanation: Scaling Efficiency: Strong scaling analysis. Speedup vs GPUs (ideal: linear). Efficiency = speedup/N. Near-linear (2-8 GPUs), sub-linear (16+). Communication overhead.

quiz.question: Model parallelism ne zaman kullanılır?
options: Model too large (single GPU memory'e sığmaz, >80GB A100). Model split (tensor/pipeline)
quiz.explanation: Model parallelism: Model çok büyük (GPT-3: 175B, 700GB). Single GPU sığmaz. Model split: Tensor parallelism (layers), pipeline (stages). Memory ↓.

quiz.question: AllReduce ne yapar?
options: Gradients'ları tüm GPUs'ta aggregate (sum/average), sonuç her GPU'ya broadcast. Sync weights
quiz.explanation: AllReduce: Collective op. Her GPU'dan gradients → aggregate (sum/average) → broadcast (her GPU'ya). Sync weights. DDP core. Ring AllReduce: O(M/B).

quiz.question: Linear scaling rule nedir?
options: Batch size ↑ → LR ∝ batch size. Distributed: Global batch büyür, LR scale et. Warmup
quiz.explanation: Linear scaling: LR_new = LR_base × (Batch_new / Batch_base). Distributed: Batch 256→2048 (8 GPU) → LR 0.1→0.8. Warmup (first few epochs). Convergence preserve.

quiz.question: Pipeline parallelism bubble nedir?
options: Idle time: Initial stages fill pipeline (forward), final stages wait. Bubble = (p-1)/m, p=stages, m=micro-batches
quiz.explanation: Pipeline bubble: Idle time (stages wait). Initial: Fill pipeline (forward all). GPipe: ~50% bubble. 1F1B schedule: ~10% (overlap forward/backward). Micro-batches ↑ → bubble ↓.

quiz.question: ZeRO (DeepSpeed) ne yapar?
options: Optimizer states, gradients, parameters split across GPUs. Memory O(Ψ/N). Trillion-param models
quiz.explanation: ZeRO: Zero Redundancy Optimizer. ZeRO-1 (optimizer split), ZeRO-2 (+ gradients), ZeRO-3 (+ parameters). Memory O(Ψ/N) vs O(Ψ). GPT-3, LLaMA training.

quiz.question: Mixed precision training avantajları?
options: 2x memory ↓ (FP16), 2-3x speed ↑ (Tensor Cores), <1% accuracy loss. Loss scaling (underflow prevent)
quiz.explanation: Mixed precision: FP16 compute (forward/backward), FP32 master weights. Tensor Cores (2-3x faster). Memory 2x ↓. GradScaler (loss scaling). torch.cuda.amp. Accuracy ~.

quiz.question: Strong vs weak scaling?
options: Strong: Fixed problem, more GPUs → faster (T↓). Weak: Problem size ∝ GPUs (batch↑), time constant (T~)
quiz.explanation: Strong scaling: Fixed dataset/model, increase GPUs (speedup). Weak scaling: Problem size ∝ GPUs (batch size ×N), time ~ constant. Weak easier (less communication per GPU).

flashcards.back: Her GPU full model replica, batch split. Forward/backward local, gradients AllReduce (sync), optimizer step. DDP. Linear speedup (ideal).
Model split across GPUs. Tensor parallelism (layers, matrix split), pipeline (stages). Large models (>80GB). Communication: activations transfer.
Collective op. Aggregate gradients (all GPUs), broadcast result. Sync weights. Ring AllReduce: O(M/B), bandwidth-bound. DDP core.
Layers → stages (GPUs). Micro-batches (fill pipeline). F-then-B (GPipe), 1F1B (overlap). Bubble time (idle): (p-1)/m.
LR ∝ batch size. Distributed: Batch ↑ (8 GPU) → LR scale (×8). Warmup (gradual LR increase). Convergence preserve.
Zero Redundancy Optimizer. ZeRO-1 (optimizer split), ZeRO-2 (+ gradients), ZeRO-3 (+ parameters). Memory O(Ψ/N). Trillion-param models.
FP16 compute (Tensor Cores), FP32 master weights. 2-3x speedup, 2x memory ↓. GradScaler (loss scaling). torch.cuda.amp.
Simulate large batch (memory efficient). Multiple micro-batches, accumulate gradients, single optimizer step. Effective batch = micro × steps.
Fixed problem, increase GPUs → faster (speedup). Ideal: Linear (N GPUs → N× speedup). Real: Sub-linear (communication overhead).
Problem size ∝ GPUs (batch ×N). Time ~ constant (ideal). Less communication per GPU. Easier than strong scaling.
Bandwidth-optimal collective. Send chunks in ring (N-1 steps). Time: 2×(N-1)×M/(N×B) ≈ 2M/B. No bottleneck node.
One-forward-one-backward (pipeline). Overlap forward/backward across stages. Bubble ~10% (vs GPipe ~50%). Micro-batches interleaved.

commonMistakes.mistake: Batch size scaling without LR adjustment
commonMistakes.why: Distributed: Batch 256→2048 (8 GPU). Same LR → convergence poor (large batch, small LR → slow, underfitting). Accuracy drop.
commonMistakes.fix: Linear scaling rule: LR_new = LR_base × (Batch_new / Batch_base). 8 GPU → LR ×8. Warmup (first 5 epochs, gradual LR increase). Validation: Monitor loss.

commonMistakes.why: DP (torch.nn.DataParallel): Single-process, GIL bottleneck, unbalanced GPU (GPU 0 bottleneck). Slow, inefficient. Legacy API.
commonMistakes.fix: DDP (DistributedDataParallel): Multi-process, no GIL, balanced GPUs. 2-3x faster than DP. Launch: torchrun, mp.spawn. Standard practice.

commonMistakes.mistake: No gradient accumulation on limited memory
commonMistakes.why: Batch size 256 → GPU OOM (out of memory, 80GB A100). Reduce batch → convergence worse (small batch noise).
commonMistakes.fix: Gradient accumulation: Micro-batch 32 × 8 steps = effective 256. Memory efficient. Same convergence. Distributed: Effective = micro × accumulation × N_GPUs.

commonMistakes.why: 16+ GPUs: Communication time >> compute time (AllReduce dominant). Speedup plateau (sub-linear scaling). Efficiency <50%.
commonMistakes.fix: (1) Mixed precision (2x less gradient data). (2) Gradient compression (top-k, quantization). (3) Overlapping (computation + communication). (4) Pipeline parallelism (reduce AllReduce frequency). (5) Bandwidth upgrade (InfiniBand).

commonMistakes.why: Model <10GB (fits single GPU). Model parallelism: Communication overhead (activations transfer), complexity ↑. Slower than data parallelism.
commonMistakes.fix: Model parallelism only for large models (>80GB, GPT-3). Small models: Data parallelism (DDP). Simpler, faster, linear speedup.

commonMistakes.why: Training days-weeks (1000 GPUs). GPU failure, power outage → restart from scratch. Days lost.
commonMistakes.fix: Checkpointing: Every N steps (1000-5000), save model+optimizer state. Distributed: Rank 0 save (or sharded save). Resume: Load checkpoint, restore epoch. Fault tolerance.

commonMistakes.why: Pipeline: Micro-batch too small → many stages, high communication. Too large → bubble ↑ (few micro-batches), memory issue.
commonMistakes.fix: Tune micro-batch: (1) Start with batch / num_micro_batches = 8-16. (2) Profile bubble time (target <10%). (3) Adjust: More micro-batches → bubble ↓, communication ↑. Balance.
